input.quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, DAMAGES FOR THE LOSS OF GOODWILL, PROSPECTIVE PROFITS OR ANTICIPATED INCOME, OR DAMAGES RESULTING FROM ANY EXPENDITURES, INVESTMENTS, LEASES OR COMMITMENTS MADE BY EITHER PARTY ON ACCOUNT OF THE TERMINATION OR EXPIRATION OF THIS AGREEMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH ITS TERMS.
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated-sum or early-termination/minimum-fee provision is payable by us anywhere in the Agreement. Payment obligations (Article V user fees, the $2,500/month support fee, Supplemental Payments and taxes) are usage- or service-based consideration, not stipulated damages. Article IV (p0049) preserves only Licensor's right to receive payments for trades actually performed on early termination — no acceleration of remaining term fees — and Article XXI (p0138) imposes only return/certification duties. Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages against either party, which cuts in our favour. The two nearest-adjacent items are not Customer-payable LDs: the audit cost-shift on a >5% discrepancy (p0064) is ordinary audit cost allocation, and the payment floor in p0070 simply ties fees to recorded traded volume. The rebate/share mechanics in p0076 run to us. No redline required for this rule; the audit cost-shift and the drafting slip naming "Licensor" in p0070's floor are better addressed under the audit and payment-terms rules.

input.quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, DAMAGES FOR THE LOSS OF GOODWILL, PROSPECTIVE PROFITS OR ANTICIPATED INCOME, OR DAMAGES RESULTING FROM ANY EXPENDITURES, INVESTMENTS, LEASES OR COMMITMENTS MADE BY EITHER PARTY ON ACCOUNT OF THE TERMINATION OR EXPIRATION OF THIS AGREEMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH ITS TERMS.
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated-sum or early-termination/minimum-fee provision is payable by us anywhere in the Agreement. Payment obligations (Article V user fees, the $2,500/month support fee, Supplemental Payments and taxes) are usage- or service-based consideration, not stipulated damages. Article IV (p0049) preserves only Licensor's right to receive payments for trades actually performed on early termination — no acceleration of remaining term fees — and Article XXI (p0138) imposes only return/certification duties. Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages against either party, which cuts in our favour. The two nearest-adjacent items are not Customer-payable LDs: the audit cost-shift on a >5% discrepancy (p0064) is ordinary audit cost allocation, and the payment floor in p0070 simply ties fees to recorded traded volume. The rebate/share mechanics in p0076 run to us. No redline required for this rule; the audit cost-shift and the drafting slip naming "Licensor" in p0070's floor are better addressed under the audit and payment-terms rules.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the p0030 grant runs to Licensee alone, p0045 limits access to Licensee's own employees, p0049 permits immediate termination for any breach with no materiality or cure, p0134 auto-terminates on Change of Control and p0149 bars any transfer — i.e. the walk-away combination of at-will revocability plus excluded Affiliates/contractors.

Redline reaches the preferred position: it extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (with Licensee responsible for their compliance), confirms transfer to an M&A successor without consent and non-termination on such a transaction, and limits Licensor revocation to a material breach uncured after 30 days' notice — matching the rule's insert-affiliates / delete-revocability / add-successor-transfer guidance.

The failed 'no at-will revocation remains' check is explained by the drafting approach rather than a substantive gap: p0049/p0134 text is left in place but expressly overridden by the 'Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement' opener in the amended grant, which is a legitimate and smaller edit than rewriting four separate paragraphs; the 0.811 changed-character ratio reflects necessary additive language, not a stray rewrite.
Comment is accurate, first-person plural, cites the playbook position and offers the Affiliates-on-written-notice fallback; no misstatement of the original text.

Advisory only (not a fail): if the counterparty resists the override construct, consider companion conforming edits to Article IV (p0049), Article XX (p0134) and the assignment clause (p0149) so the surviving language does not create interpretive conflict.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS" with all express and implied warranties disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant error-free operation, conformity to documentation, or that nonconformities will be corrected. No affirmative performance warranty, warranty period, or remedy appears anywhere in the Agreement (the only other "warrants" language is Licensee-side or mutual boilerplate about counsel). This is the playbook walk-away position, so we insert an express warranty (professional and workmanlike services; 12-month software / 90-day services conformance to documentation; compliance with laws; no malicious code) with a repair, replacement or refund remedy, and carve that express warranty out of the disclaimer so it is not swallowed.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS" with all express and implied warranties disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant error-free operation, conformity to documentation, or that nonconformities will be corrected. No affirmative performance warranty, warranty period, or remedy appears anywhere in the Agreement (the only other "warrants" language is Licensee-side or mutual boilerplate about counsel). This is the playbook walk-away position, so we insert an express warranty (professional and workmanlike services; 12-month software / 90-day services conformance to documentation; compliance with laws; no malicious code) with a repair, replacement or refund remedy, and carve that express warranty out of the disclaimer so it is not swallowed.

**Finding: missing (insurance) — redline proposed and accepted.**

The Agreement has no insurance clause. The sole "insurance" reference (p0051) merely makes Licensee responsible for taxes, shipping and insurance charges — it imposes no coverage obligation on Licensor. Since SFG/E-Path FX hosts the Platform and processes our trading and account data, the playbook's standard coverages apply.

Redline: new General Provisions subsection (l) after p0159 requiring Licensor to carry CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, cyber/privacy of USD 5M, and statutory workers' compensation, for the term plus one year, with certificates on request. Fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) flagged in the comment for negotiation.

Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no insurance obligation; the only reference to "insurance" is in the fees/taxes clause (p0051) allocating shipping and insurance charges to Licensee. Licensor hosts the platform and handles Licensee trading/account data, so the playbook requires standard coverages (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp) with certificates on request. Inserted as new subsection (l) at the end of General Provisions, before the execution paragraph.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (rule LD — liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer).

I reviewed the fee architecture (Article V user-fee bands, p0050–p0070), the "Supplemental Payments" definition and enhancements section (p0074–p0084), support fees (p0086–p0095), the term/termination provisions (Articles IV, XIX–XXI) and general provisions. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "minimum", "damages", "interest" and "equal to" returned no Customer-payable stipulated sum.

Key points:
- No liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee, minimum commitment or accelerated-fee provision is payable by us. All amounts we owe are usage- or service-based consideration.
- Article IV (p0049) preserves only Licensor's right to payment for trades actually performed on early termination — no acceleration of remaining term fees; Article XXI (p0138) imposes only return and certification duties.
- Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages against either party, which works in our favour.
- Two near-misses are not LDs against us: the audit cost-shift on a >5% discrepancy (p0064) is ordinary audit cost allocation, and the payment floor in p0070 simply ties fees to recorded traded volume. The rebate/share mechanics (p0076) run to us and are welcome.

No redline proposed. Two items are worth picking up under other rules rather than this one: the audit cost-shift trigger in p0064, and the apparent drafting slip in p0070 which states the floor applies to amounts "payable by the Licensor" where the payer is us.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS" with all express and implied warranties disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant error-free operation, conformity to documentation, or that nonconformities will be corrected. No affirmative performance warranty, warranty period, or remedy appears anywhere in the Agreement (the only other "warrants" language is Licensee-side or mutual boilerplate about counsel). This is the playbook walk-away position, so we insert an express warranty (professional and workmanlike services; 12-month software / 90-day services conformance to documentation; compliance with laws; no malicious code) with a repair, replacement or refund remedy, and carve that express warranty out of the disclaimer so it is not swallowed.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert Vendor transition-assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligation into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor materials, with nothing on our own data or exit support, so we added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then delete and certify deletion. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day export right is retained.

ops.text: (c) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiry or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee Data (meaning all data, records, trade and order information and other content of Licensee or its customers stored, processed or generated in connection with Licensee's use of the Licensed Technology) in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement.
input.rationale: The agreement is a hosted FX trading technology license under which our trade and order data resides in Licensor's system, yet Article XXI's Effect of Termination provision runs only one way: we must ship back all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, and "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." There is no wind-down, transition assistance, data export/return or deletion-certification obligation on Licensor anywhere in the document (searches for data return, export and transition returned nothing; the confidentiality article at p0124-p0125 imposes duties only on Licensee). That leaves us with no right to recover our data or continuity support at exit, which is below the playbook walk-away line. We therefore insert a new subsection (c) in Article XXI requiring Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return Licensee Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and thereafter delete and certify deletion. Fallback of ninety days' assistance with the thirty-day export retained is flagged in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert Vendor transition-assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligation into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor materials, with nothing on our own data or exit support, so we added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then delete and certify deletion. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day export right is retained.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement.
input.rationale: The agreement is a hosted FX trading technology license under which our trade and order data resides in Licensor's system, yet Article XXI's Effect of Termination provision runs only one way: we must ship back all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, and "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." There is no wind-down, transition assistance, data export/return or deletion-certification obligation on Licensor anywhere in the document (searches for data return, export and transition returned nothing; the confidentiality article at p0124-p0125 imposes duties only on Licensee). That leaves us with no right to recover our data or continuity support at exit, which is below the playbook walk-away line. We therefore insert a new subsection (c) in Article XXI requiring Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return Licensee Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and thereafter delete and certify deletion. Fallback of ninety days' assistance with the thirty-day export retained is flagged in the comment.

input.quote: II. As compensation for the Licensee to use the Licensed Technology during the Initial Period, Licensee shall pay to Licensor, the following user fees:
input.rationale: The fee architecture (Art. V, ¶¶p0056–p0063 with p0066–p0070) is purely usage-based: Licensee pays a per-US$1 million traded rate set by the Monthly Notional Volume band actually reached, calculated and paid monthly in arrears. There is no committed volume, no minimum spend, no take-or-pay, no shortfall charge and no volume cap or floor imposed on Licensee's usage — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "at least/not less than" and volume-cap language return nothing of that character. The tiered table is a discount schedule that benefits us at higher volumes, not a commitment. The only fixed recurring amount is the $2,500/month Technical Support Services fee (p0086), which is consideration for services actually delivered and so falls within the preferred position ("fees are for usage or ordered services only"). The p0070 floor ("In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded ... multiplied by the applicable Fees") is a floor measured by actual traded volume, not a minimum purchase obligation. Note for the wider review (outside this rule): the 36-month Initial Period with renewal solely at Licensor's option and no Licensee termination-for-convenience right is a term/exit issue for the TERM/TERMINATION rule, but because no take-or-pay or minimum volume is attached to that term, MINCOMMIT is satisfied and no redline is warranted here.

input.quote: II. As compensation for the Licensee to use the Licensed Technology during the Initial Period, Licensee shall pay to Licensor, the following user fees:
input.rationale: The fee architecture (Art. V, ¶¶p0056–p0063 with p0066–p0070) is purely usage-based: Licensee pays a per-US$1 million traded rate set by the Monthly Notional Volume band actually reached, calculated and paid monthly in arrears. There is no committed volume, no minimum spend, no take-or-pay, no shortfall charge and no volume cap or floor imposed on Licensee's usage — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "at least/not less than" and volume-cap language return nothing of that character. The tiered table is a discount schedule that benefits us at higher volumes, not a commitment. The only fixed recurring amount is the $2,500/month Technical Support Services fee (p0086), which is consideration for services actually delivered and so falls within the preferred position ("fees are for usage or ordered services only"). The p0070 floor ("In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded ... multiplied by the applicable Fees") is a floor measured by actual traded volume, not a minimum purchase obligation. Note for the wider review (outside this rule): the 36-month Initial Period with renewal solely at Licensor's option and no Licensee termination-for-convenience right is a term/exit issue for the TERM/TERMINATION rule, but because no take-or-pay or minimum volume is attached to that term, MINCOMMIT is satisfied and no redline is warranted here.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control
input.rationale: This is a hosted FX trading technology license under which our trade and order data sits in Licensor's system, yet Article XXI's Effect of Termination runs only one way: we must ship back all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, and all of Licensor's rights survive termination. No wind-down, transition assistance, data export/return or deletion-certification obligation on Licensor appears anywhere (searches for data return, export and transition returned nothing; the confidentiality article at p0124-p0125 binds only Licensee). That leaves us with no right to recover our data or continuity support at exit, below the playbook walk-away line. We therefore insert a new subsection (c) in Article XXI requiring Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return Licensee Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and thereafter delete and certify deletion; the 90-day fallback with the 30-day export retained is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor materials, with nothing on our own data or exit support, so we added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then delete and certify deletion. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day export right is retained.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: The agreement is a hosted FX trading technology license under which our trade and order data resides in Licensor's system, yet Article XXI's Effect of Termination provision runs only one way: we must ship back all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, and "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." There is no wind-down, transition assistance, data export/return or deletion-certification obligation on Licensor anywhere in the document (searches for data return, export and transition returned nothing; the confidentiality article at p0124-p0125 imposes duties only on Licensee). That leaves us with no right to recover our data or continuity support at exit, which is below the playbook walk-away line. We therefore insert a new subsection (c) in Article XXI requiring Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return Licensee Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and thereafter delete and certify deletion. Fallback of ninety days' assistance with the thirty-day export retained is flagged in the comment.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

**Why:** The pricing structure in Article V is entirely consumption-based. Licensee pays a per-US$1 million-traded rate determined by the Monthly Notional Volume band actually reached in the month (¶¶p0056–p0063), calculated by Licensee and paid monthly in arrears (p0069–p0070). There is:

- **No committed volume or minimum spend** — the tiered table is a volume *discount* schedule that works in our favour at higher throughput, not a purchase obligation;
- **No take-or-pay or shortfall charge** — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "at least / not less than" surface nothing of that nature;
- **No volume cap or usage restriction** on Licensee beyond operating-hours access (p0032) and the Field of Use limit.

The only fixed recurring amount is the $2,500/month Technical Support Services fee (p0086), which is consideration for services actually delivered and therefore sits inside the preferred position ("fees are for usage or ordered services only"). The p0070 floor is measured against volume *actually traded*, so it is not a minimum commitment.

**One flag for the wider review (not this rule):** the 36-month Initial Period, renewable for seven years *at Licensor's option only*, with no Licensee termination-for-convenience right (p0049), is a term/exit problem to be picked up under the TERM/TERMINATION rule. It does not trigger MINCOMMIT because no take-or-pay or minimum volume is attached to that term — the length of the term costs us nothing if we stop trading on the platform.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The fee architecture (Art. V, ¶¶p0056–p0063 with p0066–p0070) is purely usage-based: Licensee pays a per-US$1 million traded rate set by the Monthly Notional Volume band actually reached, calculated and paid monthly in arrears. There is no committed volume, no minimum spend, no take-or-pay, no shortfall charge and no volume cap or floor imposed on Licensee's usage — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "at least/not less than" and volume-cap language return nothing of that character. The tiered table is a discount schedule that benefits us at higher volumes, not a commitment. The only fixed recurring amount is the $2,500/month Technical Support Services fee (p0086), which is consideration for services actually delivered and so falls within the preferred position ("fees are for usage or ordered services only"). The p0070 floor ("In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded ... multiplied by the applicable Fees") is a floor measured by actual traded volume, not a minimum purchase obligation. Note for the wider review (outside this rule): the 36-month Initial Period with renewal solely at Licensor's option and no Licensee termination-for-convenience right is a term/exit issue for the TERM/TERMINATION rule, but because no take-or-pay or minimum volume is attached to that term, MINCOMMIT is satisfied and no redline is warranted here.

**Finding submitted: MISSING (medium severity)**

**What I found.** Article XXI "Effect of Termination" (p0138) is entirely one-directional: on termination our licenses end, we must ship all Licensed Technology, API documentation and Confidential Information back to Licensor within five days and certify compliance, and "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination."

**What is absent.** Nothing anywhere in the agreement obliges Licensor to help us exit or to give our data back:
- Searches for data return, export and transition returned no results.
- The confidentiality article (p0124–p0125) imposes duties only on Licensee; there is no counterpart return obligation on Licensor.
- No wind-down heading exists in Articles XIX–XXIII or the General Provisions.

This matters because the platform is hosted — we use it to receive market data and enter trading tickets (p0033), so our trade and order records live in Licensor's systems. As drafted we would exit with no export right, which sits at or below the playbook walk-away line ("no data return").

**Redline (validated ok:true).** New Article XXI(c) inserted after p0138 requiring Licensor to: (i) provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at then-current rates on our request; (ii) return all Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format within thirty days; and (iii) thereafter delete it and certify deletion in writing. I included a short definition of "Licensee Data" inline because the agreement has no such defined term. The comment offers the fallback of ninety days' assistance, provided the thirty-day export right is preserved.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
This is a hosted FX trading technology license under which our trade and order data sits in Licensor's system, yet Article XXI's Effect of Termination runs only one way: we must ship back all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, and all of Licensor's rights survive termination. No wind-down, transition assistance, data export/return or deletion-certification obligation on Licensor appears anywhere (searches for data return, export and transition returned nothing; the confidentiality article at p0124-p0125 binds only Licensee). That leaves us with no right to recover our data or continuity support at exit, below the playbook walk-away line. We therefore insert a new subsection (c) in Article XXI requiring Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return Licensee Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and thereafter delete and certify deletion; the 90-day fallback with the 30-day export retained is offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0138: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement.

Resolved definitions:

Licensee: SOFTWARE LICENSE AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT THIS SOFTWARE LICENSE AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT ("Agreement") is made and entered into as of this 27th day of April 2009 by and between SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX, a Delaware Corporation whose principal address is 575 Madison Avenue, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10022 ("Licensor"), and 551 FX IB Associates, LLC a Delaware Limited Liability Company, whose principal address is located at 575 Madison Avenue, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10022 ("Licensee").
CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION: 1.2 "CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION" shall mean, all existing and future information, including but not limited to Software documentation, Software training and instruction manuals, data, reports, programs, methods, tapes, recorded notes, computer-generated data, tests, studies and other written documents, computer programs, proprietary trade secrets and know-how, Software, Intellectual Property Rights and any and all other information embodied in a tangible form relating to and disclosed to the Licensee in connection with this Agreement, including but not limited to those related to the Licensed Technology. The foregoing items referenced in the preceding sentence shall be deemed to be "confidential" within the meaning hereof when, and so long as it is not in possession of the Licensee prior to the disclosure thereof (except in the event same wrongfully obtained by, or wrongly disclosed to the Licensee); or is not then and does not become part of the public knowledge and literature through the fault of the Licensee.

LICENSED TECHNOLOGY: 1.9 "LICENSED TECHNOLOGY" means the Licensed Know-How and the Licensed Software, collectively.

Rendered redline:
p0138: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement.
(c) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiry or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee Data (meaning all data, records, trade and order information and other content of Licensee or its customers stored, processed or generated in connection with Licensee's use of the Licensed Technology) in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing.

Comment:
[Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor materials, with nothing on our own data or exit support, so we added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then delete and certify deletion. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day export right is retained.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — E-Path FX / SFG License Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Verified playbook findings and redline positions  
**Privileged & confidential — attorney work product**

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. The document is drafted almost entirely in the Licensor's favour, and in several respects it sits at or below our walk-away lines.

The three critical items are risk allocation, ownership and liability. Article XII is a one-way indemnity running solely to Licensor with extremely broad triggers, and Article XIII(a) affirmatively states that Licensor is not liable for claims that use of the Licensed Technology infringes third-party IP — combined with the "AS IS" disclaimer of non-infringement, we would bear 100% of third-party IP risk in technology we neither own nor control. Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, at one half of amounts paid (below our six-month floor), while our own liability, including the broad indemnity, is uncapped and there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data security, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement. Article III vests all ownership in Licensor and, read with the broad "Derivative Work" definition and the customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), sweeps deliverables we fund into Licensor's property; the Agreement is silent on ownership of our trading, order and client data.

The high-severity items concern exit and continuity. We are committed to a 36-month Initial Period renewable for seven years at Licensor's sole option, with no convenience right for us; Licensor may terminate immediately on any breach of any covenant with no materiality or cure; and Article XX(a) automatically terminates the Agreement and all of our licences on a Change of Control unless Licensor consents, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever it merely believes its interests are affected. The licence itself does not extend to our Affiliates or contractors and cannot be transferred to a successor. Article XXI's Effect of Termination is one-way: we return everything within five days, with no Licensor obligation to return, export or delete our data and no transition assistance.

Favourable or compliant positions: governing law and venue (New York law, exclusive New York jurisdiction, no arbitration) match our preferred position; there are no liquidated damages, minimum purchase commitments or MFN/pricing-parity obligations binding us; audit cost allocation and the Article XXIII bar on termination damages cut in our favour.

Two findings — exclusivity and non-compete restrictions on the Customer — did not complete verification and require manual review before we send comments.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / redline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XII; Art. XIII(a)) | Insert Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation, breach of law, Licensor-caused unauthorised access to Licensee data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with notice/control/cooperation mechanics and express carve-out from Article XIII; narrow our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our breach of applicable law, third-party claims only. Fallback: IP-only indemnity with customary exclusions, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (with Art. III, Art. VII(b), "Derivative Work" definition) | Add Licensee ownership of its data and of paid-for customization deliverables, with perpetual royalty-free licence-back for embedded Licensor IP and no joint ownership. Licensor's platform ownership preserved. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) | Make the consequential-damages exclusion and the cap mutual; reset cap to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; add uncapped Excluded Claims; confirm fee obligations are not capped damages. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions § (c); Art. XX(a) | Permit assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor without consent; make other assignments (including any Licensor assignment) subject to reasonableness with no assignment to our competitors; remove automatic termination/consent right on our Change of Control. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (with Art. IV, Art. XX) | Extend the grant to our Affiliates and contractors (we remain responsible for compliance), make it transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction, and limit revocation to uncured material breach. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. IV; Art. XIX) | Insert a Licensee convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; confirm Licensor has no reciprocal at-will right during the Initial Period. |

| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b)) | Mutualize the non-solicit; limit to personnel directly involved in performance and to 12 months from the end of that involvement. Existing general-advertising carve-out retained. |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. IV.I) | Replace the unilateral seven-year Licensor-option extension with successive 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement and a CPI/3% cap on renewal fee increases. Fallback: automatic 12-month renewals with 60-day opt-out and 5% cap. |
| 13 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Missing | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI) | Insert new Art. XXI(c): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion and certification. Fallback: 90 days' assistance with the 30-day export retained. |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX) | Add an express warranty (professional and workmanlike services; 12-month software / 90-day services conformance to documentation; compliance with laws; no malicious code) with repair-replace-refund remedy, carved out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions | No redline. New York internal law; exclusive jurisdiction of SDNY and New York state courts; no arbitration clause. |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. | No redline. No pricing-parity or best-terms obligation binds us; the only "other licensees" reference runs in our favour (Revisions made generally available). Right of First Refusal and Change of Control consent are addressed under the assignment/change-of-control rules. |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § II License Grant and Restrictions I. (Art. V) | No redline. Fees are usage-based per US$1m traded with no committed volume, minimum spend, take-or-pay or shortfall; the monthly support fee is consideration for services delivered. Term/exit concerns are captured under T4C and RENEWAL. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | General Provisions | Insert new subsection (l) requiring CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M and workers' compensation, with certificates on request. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are at or beyond our walk-away lines and, on the verified findings, should be treated as conditions to signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **Third-party IP risk (INDEMN).** No Licensor indemnity anywhere, plus an express statement in Article XIII(a) that Licensor is not liable for infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology, plus an "AS IS" disclaimer of non-infringement. This is the rule's walk-away scenario.
2. **Liability cap and mutuality (LOL-CAP).** A one-way cap at half of amounts paid is below our six-month floor, our liability is uncapped, and there are no Excluded Claims carve-outs.
3. **Change of control (ASSIGN).** Automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our Change of Control absent Licensor consent, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing, combined with a blanket bar on our assignment and no restriction on Licensor's — this combination sits at the walk-away line.
4. **No warranty (WARRANTY).** A pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no affirmative performance warranty and no remedy is the playbook walk-away position.
5. **Renewal (RENEWAL).** A seven-year extension imposed unilaterally at Licensor's option, with no notice window and no fee cap, falls in our walk-away zone and contradicts Article IV.II–III.
6. **Exit and data recovery (TRANSITION).** No right to recover our trading, order and client data from a hosted platform, and no continuity support, is below the walk-away line.
7. **Non-solicitation (NOSOLICIT).** Three years post-termination covering all Licensor and Affiliate employees exceeds our walk-away limits (no restriction beyond 24 months; none covering all Vendor personnel).
8. **Unlimited audits (AUDIT).** Audits with no frequency cap, no advance notice, no business-hours or off-site limit and no auditor confidentiality undertaking approach our walk-away position.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Clear the two open findings.** Complete manual review of the EXCLUSIVITY and NONCOMPETE rules, both of which failed verification (tool loop exceeded). We should not issue comments until we know whether the Agreement restricts our ability to use alternative FX trading technology.
2. **Issue the redline with the walk-away items grouped first.** Lead with the Licensor IP/misconduct indemnity, mutual liability cap and Excluded Claims, warranty, data ownership, change of control, renewal and transition assistance, so Licensor sees these as a single package rather than a list of preferences.
3. **Signal fallbacks selectively.** Where the playbook supplies one, we can offer it in the comment at first exchange: IP-only indemnity with customary exclusions and a 3x annual fees super-cap; automatic 12-month renewals with a 60-day opt-out and 5% cap; 90 days' transition assistance with the 30-day data export retained.
4. **Escalate the economics of exit internally.** A 36-month commitment with no convenience right, immediate Licensor termination on any breach without cure, and no data return obligation should be confirmed as acceptable by the business before we trade any of items 1–6 above.
5. **Flag drafting points for the working session.** The audit cost-shift mechanics and the reference to "Licensor" in the payment floor (identified under the LD review) should be raised under the audit and payment-terms rules rather than as damages issues.
6. **Confirm no change to compliant positions.** Governing law and venue, MFN, minimum commitments and liquidated damages require no redline; we should resist any Licensor-side amendment to the New York law and exclusive New York jurisdiction provisions."}

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are at or beyond our walk-away lines and, on the verified findings, should be treated as conditions to signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **Third-party IP risk (INDEMN).** No Licensor indemnity anywhere, plus an express statement in Article XIII(a) that Licensor is not liable for infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology, plus an "AS IS" disclaimer of non-infringement. This is the rule's walk-away scenario.
2. **Liability cap and mutuality (LOL-CAP).** A one-way cap at half of amounts paid is below our six-month floor, our liability is uncapped, and there are no Excluded Claims carve-outs.
3. **Change of control (ASSIGN).** Automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our Change of Control absent Licensor consent, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing, combined with a blanket bar on our assignment and no restriction on Licensor's — this combination sits at the walk-away line.
4. **No warranty (WARRANTY).** A pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no affirmative performance warranty and no remedy is the playbook walk-away position.
5. **Renewal (RENEWAL).** A seven-year extension imposed unilaterally at Licensor's option, with no notice window and no fee cap, falls in our walk-away zone and contradicts Article IV.II–III.
6. **Exit and data recovery (TRANSITION).** No right to recover our trading, order and client data from a hosted platform, and no continuity support, is below the walk-away line.
7. **Non-solicitation (NOSOLICIT).** Three years post-termination covering all Licensor and Affiliate employees exceeds our walk-away limits (no restriction beyond 24 months; none covering all Vendor personnel).
8. **Unlimited audits (AUDIT).** Audits with no frequency cap, no advance notice, no business-hours or off-site limit and no auditor confidentiality undertaking approach our walk-away position.

## 4. Next steps

1. **Clear the two open findings.** Complete manual review of the EXCLUSIVITY and NONCOMPETE rules, both of which failed verification (tool loop exceeded). We should not issue comments until we know whether the Agreement restricts our ability to use alternative FX trading technology.
2. **Issue the redline with the walk-away items grouped first.** Lead with the Licensor IP/misconduct indemnity, mutual liability cap and Excluded Claims, warranty, data ownership, change of control, renewal and transition assistance, so Licensor sees these as a single package rather than a list of preferences.
3. **Signal fallbacks selectively.** Where the playbook supplies one, we can offer it in the comment at first exchange: IP-only indemnity with customary exclusions and a 3x annual fees super-cap; automatic 12-month renewals with a 60-day opt-out and 5% cap; 90 days' transition assistance with the 30-day data export retained.
4. **Escalate the economics of exit internally.** A 36-month commitment with no convenience right, immediate Licensor termination on any breach without cure, and no data return obligation should be confirmed as acceptable by the business before we trade any of items 1–6 above.
5. **Flag drafting points for the working session.** The audit cost-shift mechanics and the reference to "Licensor" in the payment floor (identified under the LD review) should be raised under the audit and payment-terms rules rather than as damages issues.
6. **Confirm no change to compliant positions.** Governing law and venue, MFN, minimum commitments and liquidated damages require no redline; we should resist any Licensor-side amendment to the New York law and exclusive New York jurisdiction provisions.
